name: ArtifactsBench
description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifacts. It contains 1,825 executable queries across nine domains and uses an automated multimodal evaluation pipeline that executes artifacts in a sandbox, captures three staged screenshots, and scores outputs with checklist-guided MLLM referees.
creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
citeAs: ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation
rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was curated through a multi-stage pipeline designed for diversity, interactivity, provenance, de-duplication, contamination control, and reproducibility. Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots. Automated filters removed incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified the results. Tasks were validated for solvability and ambiguity, and revised or removed if underspecified or solvable only by brittle hacks.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Document analysis, Others
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Candidate tasks were sourced from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Two-stage de-duplication and contamination control were applied: (i) MinHash plus semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS; (ii) screenshot perceptual hashing to detect visually near-identical artifacts. Flagged items were re-authored or discarded. Difficulty was assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ LLMs to enforce a 30%/40%/30% Easy/Medium/Hard split, realized as 559/611/655. Sub-categories were tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items, prioritizing dynamics such as state changes, animations, and responsiveness. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified. Solvability validation collected candidate solutions from multiple families and pruned underspecified items. Tasks solved only by brittle hacks were revised or removed. Execution was standardized with headless Chromium (Playwright) at 1024 × 768 resolution and deterministic seeds, and three staged screenshots were captured before, during, and after scripted interaction.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. Checklists were drafted by Hunyuan-Turbos and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchored calibration and achieved Cohen's kappa >= 0.8 among annotators; the seed was reused as few-shot references to keep difficulty high and rubrics consistent. Sub-categories were tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks. For validation, 280 queries with outputs from 6 models were independently scored in a double-blind study by multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience, and the final human ground-truth score was the median of individual annotators' ratings.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Checklist calibration used a 10% manually curated seed and achieved Cohen's kappa >= 0.8 among annotators. Human validation used a double-blind protocol with randomized sample order, and agreement between automated referees and human experts was measured using pairwise consistency rate (Pair ACC). The paper reports pairwise agreement up to 90.95% and analyzes ablations with and without images, captions, and answers.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark, evaluation harness, and baseline results are open-sourced at https://artifactsbenchmark.github.io. The paper notes version stability analysis for the Gemini referee, showing that replacing the deprecated Gemini-2.5-Pro-Preview-0506 with the stable Gemini-2.5-Pro leaves conclusions unchanged. Appendix states they release dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The query quality filtering process explicitly aims to select privacy-free queries and avoid sensitive personal information such as phone numbers, addresses, or other identifiable details.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models by providing a scalable and accurate tool for evaluating interactive visual artifact generation.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that multimodal LLM referees can suffer from hallucination, prompt sensitivity, limited awareness of engineering/code quality, version drift, and potential cognitive biases in interpreting long-horizon interaction logic and dynamic visual feedback. It also notes that referee evaluation criteria may diverge from human judgments.
rai:dataLimitations: The current methodology evaluates dynamic behavior using a sequence of screenshots at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions such as multi-step workflows or nuanced game physics. The benchmark focuses on the final artifact generated in a single turn and does not assess iterative agentic refinement, self-debugging, or multi-turn development processes.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifact generation. It is used to assess model performance across visual fidelity, interactive correctness, and code quality, provide fine-grained diagnostics, compare models at scale, and validate automated rankings against human preferences and expert judgments.
